Headline: Cam Skattebo saw zero carries in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
News Snippet: Before the game, it was widely reported that the Giants would start Najee Harris with Skattebo dealing with fumbling issues to start the season. This was indeed the case as Skattebo saw zero touches and just six snaps on the day, last among all four Giants running backs. After the game, head coach

Headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-8 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
News Snippet: Fields saw a season-high eight targets, but caught just two of those passes for 19 yards. The Giants passing game behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely isn’t productive for fantasy purposes. Darnell Mooney had a carry for 20 yards while Charlie Jones caught 2-of-3 passes for 66 yards. Fields is the best option past Nabers and Likely, but he can be left on fantasy benches for Week 7 against the Texans.

Headline: Corey Kiner rushed 11 times for 57 yards in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
News Snippet: Even with Rhamondre Stevenson active and TreVeyon Henderson surprisingly playing through his ankle injury, Kiner was called on as the Patriots’ “closer,” with all 11 of his handles coming in the final 16:30 of the contest. The Patriots were winning, but the game was still in doubt. Kiner responded by continually turning his short-yardage opportunities into first downs, while he ended up leading the team in rushing. It wasn’t easy to see that one coming, but it might be difficult for coach Mike Vrabel to un-see it as neither Stevenson nor Henderson impress in their No. 1 or 2 jobs. Kiner is worth an end-of-bench stash in 14-team leagues but is not yet 12-team league relevant.

Headline: Isaiah Likely caught 6-of-11 targets for 99 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
News Snippet: Likely scored his fifth touchdown of the season and third over the last two games. He also caught a two point conversion, with all his scoring coming in the fourth quarter from J.J. McCarthy. The pass-heavy game script helped Likely salvage his fantasy day late in the game as he saw double-digit targets for the third straight game and fourth time this season. Now averaging 9.8 targets per game, Likely is squarely in the fantasy TE1 ranks heading into a tough Week 7 matchup against the Texans.

Headline: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed 14 times for 36 yards in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
News Snippet: Stevenson was not targeted in the passing game. He didn’t make any big mistakes — that would be TreVeyon Henderson with his third quarter fumble — but like Hendo, Stevenson found himself mostly on the bench late as the Pats surprisingly rode No. 3 back Corey Kiner in closeout mode. Kiner received 11 carries in the game’s final 16:30. Speaking afterward, coach Mike Vrabel literally called it a hot-hand situation. The “hot hand” is something Stevenson rarely develops, so he can ill afford this backfield becoming a three-man committee. For now, Stevenson is still the Pats’ No. 1 running back. but things just got a little dicier heading into Thursday’s short-week matchup with the Bears.

Headline: Luther Burden III caught all eight of his targets for 95 yards in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons.
News Snippet: With Caleb Williams back from a hamstring injury, Burden led the Bears with eight targets and a season-high 95 yards, mostly on short over-the-middle passes from Williams. Burden’s long play was a 25-yard catch and run. That he ran a route on just 19 of the Bears’ 45 drop backs is something of a concern going forward. With that little route involvement, Burden will have to be hyper efficient if he’s going to be a WR2/3 in fantasy formats. He should remain in lineups next week against the Patriots.

Headline: Malik Nabers caught 12-of-15 targets for 165 yards in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
News Snippet: Nabers was once again heavily involved in the Giants’ passing game, getting the first offensive touch for New York. He saw 15 targets and tallied 165 scoreless yards on the day, with over half of this yardage coming with J.J. McCarthy in the fourth quarter. It’s the third straight 100-yard game for Nabers, who is now fully ramped up from his torn ACL last year. The Giants may be debating between Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy as the starting quarterback for next week. Regardless of the starter, Nabers sees enough volume to be a borderline WR1 for Week 7 against the Texans.

Headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 14 times for 50 yards in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs, adding two catches for 28 yards.
News Snippet: Warren and Rico Dowdle, who was active after missing three games with a toe injury, split the backfield carries for the majority of this game. Warren finally pulled away from Dowdle late in the fourth quarter and overtime. Over the final 20 minutes of the contest, Warren out-carried Dowdle 7-2. He held a modest 7-5 carries advantage through three quarters. Dowdle was more efficient on the ground, but the Steelers clearly trust Warren more in all situations when push comes to shove. Warren will be in the RB2 mix when he takes on the Saints next week.

Headline: DeMario Douglas caught 7-of-8 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets, also losing a fumble.
News Snippet: Douglas followed up his best game of the season with another best game of the season, as well as the third most receiving yards of his career. His touchdown was a nine-yarder in the second quarter where the Jets’ defense simply afforded Drake Maye too much time. Things could not have been going better for “Pop” until his fourth quarter fumble at the end of a 39-yard catch-and-run. He was the victim of a classic “Peanut punch” from behind. Rather ominously, he was not targeted thereafter, though the Patriots were also in ball-control mode as they worked on draining the clock. That today’s effort came as A.J. Brown was returning from a five-week absence was promising, but the reality is that Douglas’ big box scores are likely to remain pop-up efforts rather predictable and/or weekly occurrences. He’s a shaky WR4 even with byes and injuries in full swing.

Headline: TreVeyon Henderson rushed seven times for 31 yards in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets, adding a nine-yard reception and losing a fumble.
News Snippet: Surprisingly active, Henderson was unsurprisingly disappointing. Although his lost third quarter fumble was his first of the season, it predictably landed him in the doghouse. He touched the ball just two times thereafter, and the Patriots decided to ride No. 3 running back Corey Kiner is closeout mode. Kiner took 11 carries in the final 16:30 of game time. We know Henderson has big-play ability, but now playing at less than 100 percent in a backfield that is beginning to look like a three-man ordeal, he’s not a particularly appealing RB3/FLEX heading into Thursday’s short-week date with the Bears.

Headline: Tyjae Spears notched a one-yard carry and one-yard reception in the Titans’ Week 6 win over the Colts.
News Snippet: Spears’ two touches were a new season low, though he’s now been held to three or fewer in three of the past four weeks. The Titans have decided Tony Pollard is more of an every-down back than committee member, erasing what had been low-end FLEX status for his “1B” backfield partner. Despite his supposed contingency value, Spears is droppable if you find yourself in a roster crunch.

Headline: Tony Pollard rushed 19 times for 76 yards in the Titans’ Week 6 win over the Colts.
News Snippet: Pollard was targeted only once, finishing without a reception. Pollard has somewhat surprisingly banished No. 2 Tyjae Spears to pure breather back status, but the Titans’ overall play volume and touchdown opportunities are so limited that he is still struggling to achieve weekly RB2 status. He has nevertheless shored up his RB3/FLEX floor. That is where you will find him in the Week 7 ranks against the Browns.

Headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 33-of-49 passes for 253 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Steelers’ 26-19, Week 6 overtime win over the Bucs.
News Snippet: Rodgers and the Steelers couldn’t get anything going through three quarters. They had just three points on the board and Germie Bernard check-downs were their only method of moving the ball. Even that was barely working. Running out of options, Rodgers simply started forcing the ball to DK Metcalf. He targeted Metcalf 12 times in the fourth quarter and overtime. The Steelers scored 16 points in the fourth quarter and another seven in the extra frame. Rodgers now has at least 230 yards and multiple touchdowns in four straight games. The Steelers’ pass-crazed approach under Mike McCarthy has kept him in the QB2 mix so far, and it will do so again when he faces the Saints next week.

Headline: Juwan Johnson failed to catch either of his two targets in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
News Snippet: Johnson was silent in a low-efficiency passing day for the Saints offense. The tight end position in general was a non-factor as a pass-catching group on the day. As Tyler Shough deals with broken bones in his non-throwing hand, the Saints’ passing game is tightening up and has less room for Johnson. He is a fantasy TE2 for Week 7 against the Steelers.

Headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 3-of-7 targets for 22 yards in the Titans’ Week 6 win over the Colts.
News Snippet: We suppose 3/22 isn’t an awful outcome on a day where the quarterback completed only 11 passes, but supposed targets hog Robinson is falling further and further behind No. 4 overall pick Carnell Tate, who is suddenly stacking impressive box scores and highlight-reel plays. You would like for that to eventually add an extra element to this anemic offense — and perhaps more play volume — but until it does, Robinson is looking like little more than a last-gasp WR4 in fantasy.

Headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 21 times for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 6 loss to the Titans, adding two receptions for 57 yards.
News Snippet: Taylor also lost a fumble in the opening moments of the second half that set in motion a blown 13-0 lead against arguably the worst team in football. Taylor went into a whole crowd of Titans and did not emerge with the football. These things happen, but even the littlest things have a way of costing the Colts this season. Taylor is not the problem for Indy or fantasy managers, but Daniel Jones’ poor play is making it difficult for Indy to sustain drives, and for Taylor to live up to his high-end RB1 status. The blitz-happy Vikings are a dangerous Week 7 matchup in that regard.

Headline: C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected in the second quarter of the Bills’ Week 6 game against the Raiders.
News Snippet: Instant replay showed Gardner-Johnson spitting in the direction of Brock Bowers and other Raiders players after he was seen jawing with Bowers after a play. The veteran defensive back was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct and immediately disqualified from the game, and will likely be facing a fine and suspension later in the week. The 28-year-old DB has started all five games he has appeared in this season, and entered the day with 25 tackles, two pass breakups, and one interception.

Headline: Keenan Allen caught 8-of-11 targets for 82 yards in the Colts’ Week 6 loss to the Titans.
News Snippet: Each of Allen’s targets, receptions and receiving yards were new personal bests for his embryonic Colts career. Allen is doing what he’s supposed to be doing in Indy, but that’s not true for many of his teammates. Then again, we don’t really care in fantasy football, as Allen’s WR3 checks are clearing all the same. Allen’s short-area looks will be in high demand in Week 7 as Daniel Jones tries to survive the Vikings’ blitz onslaught.

Headline: Jalon Daniels completed 22-of-43 passes for 164 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Bucs’ 26-19, Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers.
News Snippet: Daniels added 39 yards on the ground but lost a grand total of 42 yards via five sacks. Despite making a handful of big plays, Daniels’ down-to-down inaccuracy was the storyline of this game. He routinely threw passes behind Emeka Egbuka, who only caught seven passes despite seeing a whopping 16 targets on the day. Daniels also overthrew Egbuka on a long touchdown pass that could have changed the course of this game. Baker Mayfield hasn’t resumed throwing yet, meaning Daniels will likely get at least one more start. Averaging just 167 passing yards and one passing touchdown per game, Daniels will be a low-end QB2 for his Week 7 matchup versus Carolina.

Headline: Bryce Lance caught 2-of-4 targets for 9 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
News Snippet: Lance was the Saints’ WR3 against the Giants, seeing four targets on the day. He scored his first career touchdown on a two-yard pass on fourth-and-goal at the end of the first half. Despite the score, Lance is still low in the Saints’ pass-catching order and is best left on fantasy benches.

Headline: Michael Penix completed 19-of-33 for 225 yards and three touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
News Snippet: Penix was a mess in the first half, missing Drake London on what should have been an walk-in 30-yard touchdown. The Falcons abandoned the run game in the second half, facing a three touchdown deficit, and Penix threw three touchdowns in hurry-up mode. Taking five sacks on the day, Penix targeted London and Jahan Dotson heavily, connecting with Dotson on a nicely thrown 41-yard gain in the second half. This was the first multiple-TD game of Penix’s season. He’ll be a low-ceiling superflex play in Week 7 against the 49ers.

Headline: Devaughn Vele caught 3-of-6 targets for 42 yards in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
News Snippet: The Saints offense has not pushed the ball downfield over the past two weeks, leading to low-scoring outputs for Vele. He caught three passes on the day, and nearly reeled in a fourth catch on a Tyler Shough sideline overthrow in the second quarter. When the Saints aren’t in a pass-happy game script, Vele is relegated to touchdown-dependent FLEX value. He will be in the WR4 ranks against the Steelers for Week 7.

Headline: DK Metcalf caught 11-of-15 targets for 93 yards in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs.
News Snippet: Aaron Rodgers couldn’t get much going outside of check-downs for the better part of three quarters. Then, in desperation mode, Rodgers started forcing targets to his No. 1 receiver. Metcalf saw 12 targets in the fourth quarter and overtime. He turned that into 81 yards, otherwise known as nearly all of his production for the day. Metcalf’s ability to win downfield and on the boundary isn’t being maximized by Rodgers, but the team is throwing so often that Metcalf can still rack up fantasy points with ease. With a vulnerable Saints defense on deck for Week 7, Metcalf is on the WR2/3 border as we approach the midpoint of the season.

Headline: Chris Olave caught 4-of-7 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
News Snippet: Olave finished as the Saints’ leading receiver after coming into the weekend questionable with an illness. He was able to salvage his fantasy day with an 18-yard score at the beginning of the fourth quarter. Despite a season-low 43 yards receiving, Olave is still averaging just under 100 yards receiving per game this season. There is no question he belongs in the fantasy WR1 ranks heading into a Week 7 showdown against the Steelers.

Headline: Josh Downs caught 4-of-8 targets for 40 yards in the Colts’ Week 6 loss to the Titans, adding a seven-yard rush.
News Snippet: It was a rough fantasy day for Downs, who committed two terrible drops and was stopped at the one-inch line on his second quarter end-around. He was also the intended target on one of Daniel Jones’ two interceptions, though the miscue was Downs’ fault after he bobbled a ball up into the air. On top of everything, Downs also tweaked his shoulder. He did at least remain in the game. Just not looking up to the No. 1 receiver task as the Colts await Alec Pierce’s return, Downs is sadly maxing out as a low-ceiling WR3 option in fantasy leagues.

Headline: Carnell Tate caught 6-of-7 targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 6 win over the Colts.
News Snippet: Tate’s eight-yard fourth quarter score was the first of his career. He simply beat the defense to the spot in the end zone. Although the touchdown was great, it was Tate’s 19-yard grab early in the third frame that was the highlight of the day. He skied over CB Justin Walley. Playing much better football of late even as second-year QB Cam Ward struggles to return the favor, Tate has stabilized his WR3 value and will be pushing for WR2 status with injuries mounting and bye weeks in full swing.

Headline: Brian Robinson, Jr. had two rushes for one yard in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears, adding two catches for nine yards.
News Snippet: With the Falcons down by three touchdowns and abandoning the run game in the second half, Robinson had little chance of paying off as a Week 6 flex in the usually run-first Atlanta offense. Chicago snuffed out the Falcons run game and forced Michael Penix to try to beat them through the air. Robinson will be a game-script sensitive RB3 option in Week 7 against the 49ers.

Headline: CJ Donaldson rushed six times for 39 yards and a fumble in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
News Snippet: A messy Saints committee backfield had Donaldson get the second-most snaps among New Orleans running backs against the Giants. He and Alvin Kamara were the passing-down backs while Donaldson also had a 17-yard run, the longest run by a Saints running back on the day. His first-career touchdown was called back in the third quarter after he was ruled down just shy of the goal line. The 22-year-old rookie has had a surprisingly high utilization early in the season and will continue to be involved while Travis Etienne is out. Despite this, his fantasy impact will mainly be to dilute Kamara and Kendre Miller’s fantasy values. Donaldson should only be rostered in the deepest of leagues heading into Week 7.

Headline: Daniel Jones completed 22-of-42 passes for 269 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Colts’ 26-20, Week 6 loss to the Titans, adding three carries for 30 yards.
News Snippet: This one is going to leave a mark. The Colts led 13-0 at halftime but couldn’t get anything going after the break, where they committed two turnovers and Jones provided just 116 yards passing. His third quarter pick came only moments after a lost Jonathan Taylor fumble. It went right to Titans corner Cor’Dale Flott. Jones was not helped by some shaky hands from default No. 1 receiver Josh Downs, but he simply was not standing and delivering. Jones is really struggling to drive the ball this season, and he’s contributing far less than usual with his legs. In other words, he looks like a 29-year-old coming off a torn achilles’ tendon. There is little reason to expect things to get better in the near term, very much including Week 7 against Brian Flores’ ferocious Vikings defense.

Headline: Darius Cooper caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
News Snippet: With DeVonta Smith back, Cooper played just 39 of 64 snaps and ran a route on 26 of the team’s 52 dropbacks. Those were both fourth among wide receivers on the team. Cooper’s fantasy value is likely limited until there is another injury in the receiving room.

Headline: Cam Ward completed 11-of-22 passes for 102 yards, one touchdown and an interception in the Titans’ 26-20, Week 6 win over the Colts.
News Snippet: Ward added just three carries for seven yards. Ward got the “quarterback win” as the Titans finally broke their five-game losing streak to begin the season, but this was more about the Colts imploding and setting up one short Titans field after another with turnovers. Ward did keep his connection with No. 4 overall rookie Carnell Tate going, finding him for 6/70/1 on seven targets. Ward didn’t find veteran Calvin Ridley for what would have been a wide open end zone grab, but we digress. His interception was a second quarter sail job as he was getting leveled by the blitz. Ward’s increasing chemistry with Tate is the Titans’ first real good news of the season, but today was not a particularly inspiring victory. They now get the Browns for a Week 7 home matchup.

Headline: Kyle Pitts caught 5-of-7 targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
News Snippet: Pitts was one of the beneficiaries of a pass-heavy second half for a Falcons offense that was forced to abandon the run game facing a multi-touchdown deficit. Pitts took advantage of single coverage a couple times, including on his first touchdown grab. He now has three touchdowns over his past two games as Michael Penix brings some stability to the Atlanta offense. Pitts, who ran a route on 26 of the team’s 38 drop backs against Chicago, will be a viable play in Week 7 against the Niners.

Headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-6 targets for 19 yards in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
News Snippet: Despite not lighting up the box score, Lemon was third on the team in targets and finished fourth in receptions. Initial reports had him playing on 52 of the team’s 64 snaps and running a route on 47 of their 52 dropbacks. That was the most routes of any receiver on the team. Some of this was because the team seemed to be easing DeVonta Smith back from injury, and Dontayvsion Wicks briefly left the game with an injury scare, but we also wouldn’t be surprised to see Lemon get more work in what is looking like a bit of a lost season in Philadelphia.

Headline: Kendre Miller rushed 20 times for 70 yards in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
News Snippet: Milles led the Saints backfield in snaps and touches, adding two receptions for zero yards to his 70 scoreless rushing yards. He is the clear lead runner for the Saints and was tackled at the one-yard line on two separate drives, coming up just short of a touchdown to salvage his fantasy day. Miller’s lack of involvement in the passing game caps his fantasy ceiling but rushing volume makes him a low-end RB3 for Week 7 against a solid Steelers defense.

Headline: Emeka Egbuka caught 7-of-16 targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in the Bucs’ Week 6 loss to the Steelers.
News Snippet: Fantasy managers can’t complain about 17.8 PPR points, but this should have been an explosion spot for the second-year wideout. Jalon Daniels routinely missed him on routine throws, the most painful of which was a long would-be touchdown that grazed Egbuka’s hands as it sailed past him. There were several other throws that were behind, low, or simply too late. A short, two-yard score at the top of the second quarter will have to suffice. Egbuka is pulling away as the Bucs’ alpha receiver, pushing him back into the WR2 ranks for the team’s Week 7 date with the Panthers.

Headline: Dontayvion Wicks caught 2-of-4 targets for 24 yards in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
News Snippet: Wicks wasn’t much of a factor in this one. Tanner McKee seemed far more comfortable throwing to DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert, which left few targets for Wicks. Initial reports have Wicks playing on 40 of the team’s 64 snaps and running a route on 32 of their 52 dropbacks, which was actually fewer than Makai Lemon and only five more than Darius Cooper. Some of that could be because Wicks grabbed at his ankle and left the field after a tackle in the second half. He was able to return to the game later in the half, but he missed a few plays while being tended to by trainers. With McKee at quarterback, it’s hard to trust Wicks in fantasy, regardless of matchup.

Headline: Dallas Goedert caught 6-of-8 targets for 61 yards in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
News Snippet: Early in the game, when Tanner McKee was struggling to get anything going, he seemed locked onto Goedert. When the Panthers were up by multiple scores and the defense seemed to allow some more space in the secondary, McKee felt more confident in taking shots down the field to his receivers, which meant Goedert was quiet in the second half. Still, he was second on the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards and will be a low-end TE1 against the Cowboys next week.

Headline: Ladd McConkey (head) was ruled out in Week 6 against the Chiefs.
News Snippet: McConkey exited the game after a 17-yard reception in the first quarter and was seen entering the blue medical tent before being helped to the locker room. The quickness with which he was ruled out could mean the injury is on the severe side. The Chargers are down to their fifth and sixth wideouts on the depth chart. Justin Herbert likely won’t be fantasy relevant for the rest of the season.

Headline: DeVonta Smith caught 7-of-14 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
News Snippet: Smith was easily the focal point of the passing attack after coming back from injury. He saw the most targets of anybody on the team by six, but many of them were not catchable. However, Tanner McKee kept taking shots down the field, and he made a beautiful pass to Smith in the end zone for a touchdown. The game itself might not be pretty when McKee is under center, but it seems like Smith is going to see the volume to continue producing solid fantasy value. He’s a low-end WR2 in a good matchup against the Cowboys next week.

Headline: Omar Cooper Jr. caught 6-of-7 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
News Snippet: Active for the first time since Week 1, the No. 30 overall pick shook off his ankle issue by recording the first 100-yard outing of his now two-game career. It was a much needed effort with No. 1 Garrett Wilson getting tangled up in Christian Gonzalez’s coverage. The highlight was a 48-yard touchdown where Cooper got behind the entire defense then came back to an underthrown deep ball for six. This was after he had a shorter touchdown called back by a dubious Tim Patrick OPI penalty. Now firmly in the mix for No. 2 status even when Adonai Mitchell comes back from his seemingly never-ending finger injury, Cooper is worth rostering in a majority of fantasy leagues with injuries mounting and bye weeks raging. The Jets have a plus Week 7 matchup in the Dolphins.

Headline: Germie Bernard caught 11-of-12 targets for 87 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs.
News Snippet: Bernard began the game with a potentially catastrophic blunder by moving the chains on first down, only to run back behind the sticks in search of more yards. He was taken down behind the line to gain for a turnover on downs. Instead of banishing him to the bench, Aaron Rodgers continued to lean on the rookie throughout the contest for easy completions underneath. He tied DK Metcalf for a team-high in catches. Per the broadcast, it was the most catches by a rookie receiver of Rodgers since the grizzled veteran entered the league. Bernard went from a PPR scam to a full-blown breakout in overtime by extending the ball for a game-winning touchdown with two defenders draped over him. Bernard has 21 targets over the past two weeks. He also has at least 80 yards in back-to-back games. He is looking at a WR3 ranking for his Week 7 matchup with the Saints.

Headline: Dameon Pierce rushed 12 times for 35 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
News Snippet: With Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, and Will Shipley all hurt, and Carson Steele getting injured early in this game, Pierce took every single carry for the Eagles on Sunday. He also played on 61 of the team’s 64 snaps. However, that wasn’t able to amount to much on the ground with all of Philadelphia’s injuries. Pierce was also asked to pass block a lot, which means he only ran a route on 15 of the team’s 52 dropbacks. That’s going to limit his fantasy value, and he looks like a TD-dependent FLEX play while he remains the starter. The upside is that there doesn’t seem to be anybody coming for his job until Barkley (hamstring) returns.

Headline: Jahan Dotson caught 3-of-5 targets for 87 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
News Snippet: Dotson, whose season-high yardage coming into the week was 54 — his total in both of the past two weeks — got loose a couple times in this one, mostly when the Falcons ditched their usual run-heavy offense in favor of a fast-pace pass-heavy approach while facing a multiple touchdown second half deficit. Running a route no 32 of the Falcons’ 38 drop backs, Dotson led the team in receiving yards thanks largely to a 41-yard grab. Dotson could be a deep league play in Week 7 against the Niners.

Headline: Darren Waller did not have a catch on two targets in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
News Snippet: Initial reports have Waller playing on 36 of the team’s 79 snaps and running a route on 21 of their 46 dropbacks. Tommy Tremble, the other tight end, ran a route on 14 dropbacks, so Waller is technically the primary option in the passing game of the two. However, Tremble scored two touchdowns this week. We don’t recommend chasing either guy in fantasy right now.

Headline: Geno Smith completed 20-of-30 passes 252 yards, one touchdown and an interception in the Jets’ 26-19, Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
News Snippet: Smith was missing Adonai Mitchell for the fourth consecutive contest, but he found returning rookie first-rounder Omar Cooper Jr. for a sizzling 6/103/1 on seven targets. That was a necessary development with Garrett Wilson being limited to 4/44 as he was hounded by Christian Gonzalez. The 252 yards were Smith’s second most of the season, though his first interception of 2026 was a dreadful, costly mistake in the fourth quarter. He threw it in Keyon Sadiq’s direction, but Charles Woods ran the rookie tight end’s route for him. Disappointing, though we now have six games of evidence that Smith isn’t the bottom-three QB he appeared to be amidst the Raiders’ 2025 fiasco. Things could also get better if Mitchell soon returns and forms a legit trio with Wilson and Cooper. Smith won’t rise above mid-range QB2 status even for premium matchups, but he does have a primo Week 7 spot in the Dolphins.

Position: Concepcion caught 4-of-6 targets for 37 yards in the Browns’ Week 6 win over the Ravens, adding two carries for two additional yards.
Headline: KC Concepcion caught 4-of-6 targets for 37 yards in the Browns’ Week 6 win over the Ravens, adding two carries for two additional yards.
News Snippet: Concepcion’s six targets led all Browns players, while his 37 receiving yards were good for second-most behind Jerry Jeudy. Concepcion’s biggest play of the game came on a 17-yard reception in the third quarter that helped set up the Browns’ first scoring drive of the afternoon. Concepcion had a red zone carry inside the Ravens’ 10-yard line that resulted in only a one-yard gain, but it’s always good to see his coaches trusting him in the valuable areas of the field. We are still waiting on his first breakout game, but the volume continues to be encouraging. Concepcion will be a fringe WR3/WR4 next week against the Titans.

Headline: Tommy Tremble caught all four of his targets for 46 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
News Snippet: The Panthers seemed a little concerned about the Eagles’ pass rush since Tremble played on 54 of the team’s 79 snaps. He also was on the field for more than half of their dropbacks, but a large chunk of those were in pass-blocking situations. Still, he was schemed wide open on both touchdown passes, which led to a great fantasy day. It’s just not something we would recommend chasing next week.

Headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-9 passes for 86 yards in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
News Snippet: McMillan saw a lot of Quinyon Mitchell in tight coverage on Sunday, but he had a solid day that could have been much better after a fourth-quarter pass went off his hands in the end zone. It would have been a difficult catch with Mitchell draped all over him, but it was a catchable pass. More importantly, it shows that McMillan remains a key piece of this passing game, and he did run the most routes of any receiver on the team.

Headline: Caleb Williams completed 30-of-36 attempts for 305 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons, adding four rushes for three yards.
News Snippet: Williams was all the way back in this one, returning to action after three weeks on the sideline recovering from a hamstring injury. His only real miss of the day came on a ten yard throw to Colston Loveland that should have been an easy touchdown. Williams tormented the pass-funnel Atlanta defense with middle-of-the-field throws, along with typical out-of-structure passes to the sideline. It was an impressive outing against a Falcons defense giving up the league’s fifth lowest drop back success rate. Williams should remain in lineups in Week 7 against the Patriots.

Headline: Nolan Smith has been ruled out of Week 6 against the Panthers with a concussion.
News Snippet: Smith was on a pass rush rep, coming off the edge, when he got hit hard under the chin on a chip block by Chuba Hubbard. There was no helmet-to-helmet contact, but Smith went down hard and was immediately evaluated for a concussion. He was later ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Headline: Brenton Strange caught 5-of-7 targets for 44 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
News Snippet: The Jaguars did have a tight end touchdown, but unfortunately for fantasy managers it went to Nate Boerkircher on a ridiculous one-handed stab on a pop pass at the goal line. Strange has now gone for 23 targets in three games and appears to be crowding out Brian Thomas Jr. He’s a reasonable low-end TE1, albeit one on bye next week.

Headline: Brian Thomas Jr. failed to catch either of his two targets in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
News Snippet: That’s three games with three or fewer targets and Thomas Jr. has put up back-to-back bagels in London, apparently distraught over the local cuisine. He absolutely does not have to be rostered in most fantasy leagues through Jacksonville’s Week 7 bye.

Headline: Travis Hunter caught 4-of-4 targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
News Snippet: In London, where Travis Hunter’s best games live, Hunter both caught a touchdown and picked off C.J. Stroud (his first of the season), becoming the first player to do both in the same game since Brian Dawkins in 2002. Hunter did all this on just nine offensive snaps. The skill is there to do this on offense, but the Jaguars have really been defense-first with his snaps this year. Depending on the post-bye buzz, Hunter could be a reasonable pick-up in fantasy leagues ahead of Week 8’s games.

Headline: Parker Washington caught 4-of-11 targets for 64 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
News Snippet: A lot of these incompletions were balls Washington got a hand on but couldn’t quite reel in as was breaking to the sideline. Washington displayed his speed and shiftiness on a 27-yard catch-and-run in the second quarter where he cut through both Texans linebackers for a big gain. He is a fantasy WR2 as the Jaguars enter their bye week. Washington is #onpace for a near-1,200 yard season with 14 touchdowns even after this dud.

Headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is questionable to return to Week 6 against the Eagles.
News Snippet: Phillips came into this game questionable with a hamstring injury but was able to suit up. Unfortunately, he got hurt early in the first quarter and is unlikely to return. Considering he had the bye week to heal and is not 100 percent, it seems likely that the EDGE rusher will miss some time with the injury.

Headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 5-of-10 targets for 83 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
News Snippet: It’s his highest target total of the season and the first time Meyers has managed 10 targets since Week 14 of the 2025 season. No touchdown here, but Meyers is a fine real-life third receiver who has mostly been left to the FLEX life in Jacksonville. He enters the bye as someone who can be dropped in shallow leagues in a roster crunch, but also someone solidly in the top 50 wideouts in the league on a good offense.

Headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed 11 times for 55 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
News Snippet: He failed to catch his only target. Rodriguez was churning out success rate on the regular in the first half. The Jaguars curiously went away from him in the second half, as he played just 21-of-70 snaps and had only one carry after halftime. He’s not a must-hold through the bye week, but this game is the proof-of-concept that he can be an effective weapon for the Jaguars if they want to use him as a between-the-tackles pounder.

Headline: Romeo Doubs injured his shoulder in the Patriots’ Week 6 game against the Jets and is questionable to return.
News Snippet: Doubs landed hard on his shoulder on his first reception, which just happened to be a 42-yard touchdown where he broke free along the back line of the defense. Most unfortunate, though he at least tallied the score first. Doubs was evaluated in the blue tent before heading to the locker room. Perhaps he will return, but he is probably on the wrong side of questionable. It’s bad news for the Pats and fantasy managers, but at least comes as A.J. Brown is back in the lineup for the first time in five weeks.

Headline: Carson Steele left Week 6 against the Panthers with a shoulder injury.
News Snippet: Steele caught a screen pass in the flats and lowered his head to try and run over the defender. He came up holding his shoulder and had to have the shoulder immobilized as he walked into the locker room with his pads off. It had the look of a dislocation, which would mean Dameon Pierce and Jaydon Blue are the only two healthy running backs for the Eagles.

Headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 12 times for 39 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans, adding four catches for 48 yards and two touchdowns on his only four targets.
News Snippet: The Jaguars looked like they were in control with their run game early in this one, but Tuten sputtered out in the second half, where he managed just six carries for 18 yards with the Jaguars curiously going away from Chris Rodriguez Jr. Tuten played 40-of-72 snaps with Rodriguez having a big day on the ground. It feels good that his “down” games are like this, and he also had a rushing touchdown pulled off the board after what appeared to be a phantom holding flag was thrown. Tuten enters the Week 7 bye as an RB2.

Headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 24-of-41 passes for 306 yards, four touchdowns and one interception in Jacksonville’s 34-31, Week 6 loss to the Texans.
News Snippet: It could have been more, had Liam Coen not settled for a game-tying field goal on fourth-and-short with less than four minutes left in the game. It also could have been more had Lawrence not thrown an end-zone pick to Calen Bullock. At the end of the day, the screen day was dealing and Lawrence was hitting all sorts of in-breakers against a beleaguered Texans secondary. He enters the bye week as a sure-fire QB1 with 1,174 passing yards and 10 throwing touchdowns in his first five games. Last year’s rushing touchdowns appear to have vanished as the Jaguars have gotten better in the red zone, but Lawrence is still playing exceptional football.

Headline: Foster Moreau caught 2-of-2 targets for seven yards and two touchdowns in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
News Snippet: Sure. One of them was even a beautiful one-handed snag as the game drew near halftime. Moreau out-paced Dalton Schultz (4-of-6 targets, 33 yards) in the fantasy streets even if not on the snap count spreadsheets. You know better than to chase the low-snap high-touchdown outlier.

Headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught 3-of-4 targets for 34 yards in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
News Snippet: It tied his season-high for receptions in four games with Arizona. Harrison played just 12 snaps. The Texans do seem dedicated to giving him the ball — as you’d hope after he was acquired for a second-round pick — and we imagine he’ll be in the FLEX conversation next week against the Giants after a full week to hone trust with the coaching staff. His first two catches were on in-breaking routes.

Headline: Nico Collins caught 3-of-5 targets for 76 yards in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
News Snippet: He added a long defensive pass interference penalty drawn on Travis Hunter to set up Houston’s second third-quarter touchdown. Collins also took an end around in the red zone for five rushing yards. Close, but ultimately not the line that fantasy managers were hoping for. Collins will remain in the low-end WR1 region against the Giants in Week 7.

Headline: Jaylin Noel caught 4-of-4 passes for 107 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
News Snippet: Noel has scored in all of Houston’s wins this year; that’s analytics. The underlying numbers are more annoying — he played 31-of-63 snaps and was not one of Houston’s top targets in what has been a frustrating room. Still, it’s very clear he’s the second-most talented player in this receiving corps, even if Marvin Harrison Jr. is cutting in. Noel has some FLEX viability in Week 7 against the Giants.

Headline: Jawhar Jordan rushed six times for 43 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars, adding a seven-yard reception on his only target.
News Snippet: Jordan had a huge cutback lane in the third quarter and took it 25 yards while breaking a Jarrian Jones tackle for his touchdown. He played just 14-of-63 snaps, but clearly brought more juice than Woody Marks in the run game and it wouldn’t be a total surprise if that total grew next week with David Montgomery (groin) expected to remain sidelined. Jordan is likely just a FLEX play against the Giants in Week 7.

Headline: Woody Marks rushed 15 times for 56 yards in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars, adding two catches for 25 yards on three targets.
News Snippet: Marks was mostly bottled up, though he did manage 9/41 in the second half behind a few reasonably big runs to become the first back all year to hit 40 rushing yards against the Jaguars. He played 49-of-63 snaps. The Texans run game is still bad, but against the Giants in Week 7 Marks should probably be on the RB2 line.

Headline: C.J. Stroud completed 24-of-34 passes for 312 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in Houston’s 34-31, Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
News Snippet: The Texans running game was mostly abandoned until the fourth quarter, leaving Stroud to wail on an overmatched Jaguars secondary. His best throw was probably on Houston’s final possession of the first half, as he dotted a 50-yard throw with a defender in his face to Jaylin Noel, eventually setting up (checking notes) Foster Moreau’s second touchdown of the day. Stroud has now thrown for six touchdowns and gone over 260 yards in each of his last three games; he’s suddenly in the high-end QB2 competition with bye weeks hitting as the Texans host the Giants in Week 7.

Headline: Reed Blankenship (concussion) was ruled out of Houston’s Week 6 game against the Jaguars.
News Snippet: Blankenship suffered the concussion near the end of the first half and was carted off with a towel over his head. MJ Stewart took over at safety for a suddenly-ordinary Texans defense.

Headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is active for Week 6 against the Falcons.
News Snippet: Williams will make his return to the starting lineup after being sidelined for a few weeks with a hamstring injury while the Bears declared RB Kyle Monangai, CB Tyrique Stevenson, LB T.J. Edwards, LB Keyshaun Elliott, OL Jordan McFadden, DL Jayden Loving, and QB Case Keenum inactive against Atlanta. Monongai’s absence should translate into another big workload for D’Andre Swift, facing a tough Falcons rush defense. Meanwhile, Tyson Bagent will serve as Williams’ backup.

Headline: Giants declared TE Theo Johnson, CB Colton Hood, QB Jake Haener, S Tyler Nubin, OL Jermaine Eluemunor, and DL C.J. Okoye inactive for Week 6 against the Saints.
News Snippet: Johnson was declared out heading into the weekend with a neck injury. Also out due to injury are Hood (concussion), Eluemunor (calf), and Nubin (neck). Expect to see more Thomas Fidone behind Isaiah Likely at the tight end position with Johnson out against the Saints.

Headline: Michael Penix (ribs) is active for Week 6 against the Bears.
News Snippet: Penix was able to practice this week and will start for Atlanta in a potentially high scoring game against the Bears. Penix should be considered a streaming option in most formats. Falcons declared QB Cooper Rush, QB Jack Strand, CB C.J. Henderson, DB Malcolm DeWalt IV, LB Christian Harris, OL Ethan Onianwa, and DE Drake Jackson inactive against the Bears.

Headline: Pat Freiermuth (calf) is active for Week 6 against the Bucs.
News Snippet: Muth was a late addition to the injury report, with the Steelers adding him on Saturday and listing him as questionable. With multiple starting receivers out this week, Muth will be asked to take on more work as a pass-catcher, moving him up the TE2 ranks. Inactive for the Steelers are WR Ben Skowronek, QB Drew Allar, QB Will Howard, CB Sean Murphy-Bunting, RB Eli Heidenreich, CB Terell Smith, and DL Kevin Jobity Jr.

Headline: Rico Dowdle (toe) is active for Week 6 against the Bucs.
News Snippet: Dowdle is back after missing three games with the toe issue. He will form a committee with Jaylen Warren, but the latter’s elite play last week likely earned him a larger split of the backfield in Week 6. Dowdle will primarily operate between the tackles, pushing him to the back of the RB3 ranks.

Headline: Panthers declared OT Monroe Freeling, TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, RB AJ Dillon, OG Torricelli Simpkins, OT Albert Reese, and DT TeRah Edwards inactive for Week 6 against the Eagles.
News Snippet: The good news is that offensive tackle Taylor Moton is active for the first time this year. He missed the first month of the season while recovering from treatment for a blood clot. He will start at right tackle in place of Freeling.

Headline: Saints declared RB Alvin Kamara (back) active for Week 6 against the Giants.
News Snippet: Kamara is active after NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported he would be expected to play in Week 6. He played through the back injury last week and is part of a rough running back committee in the Saints backfield. Kamara is in the RB4 ranks for fantasy purposes. Also active is Chris Olave (illness). The Saints declared QB Zach Wilson, EDGE Anfernee Jennings, S Mike Reid, LB Kaden Elliss, DT Nathan Shepherd, and DT John Ridgeway inactive for Week 6 against the Giants.

Headline: Ravens declared QB Lamar Jackson, WR Elijah Sarratt, FS K’Von Wallace, C Cam Jurgens, OG Andrew Vorhees, TE Matthew Hibner, and DE Broderick Washington inactive for Week 6 against the Browns.
News Snippet: The Ravens didn’t have any players listed as questionable entering the weekend, so all of these players are either healthy scratches or were ruled out before Sunday. The Ravens will start Tyler Huntley for the second consecutive week as Jackson continues to recover from the ankle injury he suffered in Week 4 against the Titans.

Headline: Eagles declared WR Hollywood Brown, RB Saquon Barkley, S Michael Carter II, EDGE A.J. Epenesa, EDGE Jalyx Hunt, and QB Joe Milton inactive for Week 6 against the Panthers.
News Snippet: Despite the Eagles’ absurdly lengthy injury report, they only had one player listed as questionable for Week 6. That was center Drew Kendall, who is active. Brown was dealing with an ankle issue earlier this week but was cleared from the injury report on Friday, making him a healthy scratch.

Headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is active for Week 6 against the Jets.
News Snippet: As are A.J. Brown (ankle) and LT Will Campbell (knee). It’s a rare day where all the injury news went right for a team. We can’t imagine Henderson will be in large for a particularly big backup role behind Rhamondre Stevenson, but the fact that a player the Pats didn’t even really “need” for Week 6 is giving it a go suggests he is close to regular health. Henderson is a boom/bust FLEX option. Inactive for the Patriots are CB Carlton Davis, CB Karon Prunty, QB Behren Morton, CB Channing Canada, OT Dametrious Crownover and TE Tanner Arkin.

Headline: Colts TE Tyler Warren is inactive for Indianapolis’ Week 6 game against the Titans.
News Snippet: Warren suffered a groin injury during Friday’s practice and was put on the questionable line; this is not great news for his chances of playing in Week 7’s game. Fantasy managers relying on Warren must immediately pivot elsewhere. Also inactive for the Colts are WR Ashton Dulin, LB Jaylon Carlies, QB Riley Leonard (third quarterback), and G Dalton Tucker.

Headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is active for Week 6 against the Patriots.
News Snippet: Sadiq made quick work of the league’s concussion protocol, for better or worse. With Omar Cooper Jr. also active vs. the Pats, Sadiq isn’t much more than a low-end TE2 prayer.

Headline: Omar Cooper (ankle) is active for Week 6 against the Patriots.
News Snippet: Up for the first time since Week 1, Cooper should immediately slide in as the Jets’ No. 2 wideout with Adonai Mitchell (finger) still somehow on the shelf. He’s a dart throw WR4 for a contest where the Jets should be playing from behind. Joining Mitchell on the shelf for Gang Green are RB Breece Hall, CB Nahshon Wright, LG Dylan Parham, DT Jack Heflin and EDGE Joseph Ossai.

Headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will not play in Week 6 against the Ravens.
News Snippet: Judkins tested out his ankle in pregame warmups, with the team deciding afterward that he would not play in this AFC North battle with the Ravens. With backup Dylan Sampson still sidelined and Raheim Sanders (hip) on injured reserve, the Browns will look to Jaleel McLaughlin and the recently signed Audric Estime to lead their backfield in Week 6. This is looking like a backfield to avoid for this week, but McLaughlin could have some value in deeper leagues. The Browns also ruled QB Taylen Green, CB Noah Igbinoghene, DT Mike Hall Jr., C Parker Brailsford, OG Teven Jenkins, and DT Mason Graham inactive for this week.

Headline: Azeez Al-Shaair left Houston’s Week 6 game against the Jaguars to be evaluated for a concussion.
News Snippet: The Jaguars have been able to impose their will on the Texans in the run game in the first half, and this won’t help matters. Al-Shaair left after Jacksonville scored their first touchdown in the second quarter and was spotted walking to the locker room. He returned towards the beginning of the second half.

Headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to play “a good amount” in Week 6 against the Jets.
News Snippet: Brown was activated from injured reserve this week and will suit up versus the Jets. It was reasonable to expect some sort of snap count in his first game back, but it sounds like Brown will be a full-go after looking great in practice this week. In desperate need of a true WR1 to step up, the Pats should pepper Brown with targets this week. He is back in the fantasy WR2 ranks after the lengthy absence.

Headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Commanders owner Josh Harris “would love” for Dan Quinn to remain the team’s head coach.
News Snippet: Garafolo says this as if Harris is simply a bystander watching Quinn bumble his way through another season. Garafolo did add that “anything is on the table” if the Commanders get blown out by the 49ers on national television on Monday. They are currently 7.5-point underdogs on most sportsbooks. With a bye week on deck after San Francisco, the Commanders could see Week 7 as the best time to pull the plug on Quinn.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that “no change is imminent” at head coach for the Saints.
News Snippet: Saints owner Gayle Benson said earlier this week that the team’s 1-4 record is “not acceptable.” Rapoport noted that she came to practice in a “show of support” for Moore and company, though it felt equally like a show of force from the outside. Rapsheet also stressed several times that the team needs to start winning games. While a change at head coach might not happen next week, it does sound like Moore won’t survive the season if things don’t turn around soon.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Najee Harris is “set to start” for the Giants in Week 6 against the Saints.
News Snippet: , who said Harris is “likely to have a larger role with Cam Skattebo downgraded but still part of the mix after the fumbles.” Skattebo has indeed struggled with fumbles, putting the ball on the ground four times this year. No running back has more fumbles, and Skattebo’s most recent blunder cost the Giants a shot at an overtime win versus the Commanders last week. They instead settled for a tie. Even if Skattebo winds up leading the team in carries this week, he was only valuable for fantasy managers because of his high-volume role. With that out the window, Skattebo is buried in the RB3 ranks for Week 6.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Rico Dowdle (toe) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Bucs.
News Snippet: Dowdle has been out since Week 2 because of the toe issue. In the meantime, Jaylen Warren has looked like one of the league’s most dynamic backs on the ground and through the air. While his gargantuan workload will return to normal with Dowdle back, Warren should still operate as the team’s unquestioned RB1. Dowdle is just a mid-range FLEX play for his first game back.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler Jr. (ankle) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Packers.
News Snippet: JPJ was downgraded to a limited participant in Friday before being hit with the questionable tag, causing some concern about his Week 6 availability. It looks like the light practice session may have been a precaution. The newly-minted Cowboys should be good to go versus Green Bay.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Tyler Warren (groin) is a game-time decisions for Week 6 against the Titans.
News Snippet: Warren suffered the groin injury during Friday’s practice. He was added to the injury report and listed as questionable for Week 6. Of note, Warren also dealt with a groin injury late in training camp, though he was ready to go for Week 1 and had not appeared on the injury report again until this week. Even if he does suit up, Warren will be at far less than 100 percent. Expect Josh Downs and Keenan Allen to take on more work whether or not Warren is active.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Tyler Shough has two broken bones in his non-throwing hand.
News Snippet: Both Shough and Kellen Moore have given non-answers when asked about the quarterback’s left hand. Per Schefter, the injury could take a couple of months to heal, but it will not cost him any playing time. Shough injured his hand versus the Falcons in Week 4 and wore a protective glove in Week 5. He is coming off his two worst games of the year, though we don’t suspect the hand is to blame. Things get much easier this week with the Giants on tap. Shough will get another shot at a QB1 finish in Week 6.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Joe Alt (neck) is expected to “ramp up” this week.
News Snippet: Pre Rapoport, Alt received good news after seeing a specialist for his neck injury earlier this week. Alt missed last week’s game with the issue and has already been ruled out for Week 6, but this is still a positive turn of events, all things considered. With a Week 7 bye on deck, Alt could be back as soon as the following week when the Bolts take on the Rams.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Steelers are “optimistic” Pat Freiermuth (calf) will play in Week 6 against the Bucs.
News Snippet: Freiermuth was added to the injury report on Saturday. The team listed him as questionable for Week 6. A last-minute addition to the injury report is never a good sign, so we wouldn’t be surprised if his snaps are limited even if he is active. On the other hand, with Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman out, the Steelers may have no choice but to play a banged-up Muth more than expected. He will be a high-risk TE2 if active.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
News Snippet: Sadiq left Week 5 with a concussion. He was upgraded to a full practice on Friday and seemingly cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend. With Mason Taylor and Omar Cooper Jr. back for Week 6, there will likely be fewer targets to go around in a Jets offense that has regressed heavily over the past two weeks. Sadiq is a low-end TE2 for his date with New England.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Abdul Carter (groin) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Saints.
News Snippet: Carter got in one limited practice to close the week before being listed as questionable. That would normally make him a coin-flip at best to play today, head coach John Harbaugh was optimistic about Carter’s health early in the week. He is good to go, as is left tackle Andrew Thomas, who is dealing with a groin injury. He has played through the groin issue several times already and will do so again versus the Saints.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sean Tucker (quad) is not expected to play in Week 6 against the Steelers.
News Snippet: Despite seeing just eight total carries this year, Tucker has two attempts inside the five compared to one for Bucky Irving. Though he isn’t leaving that many total carries behind, Tucker’s absence will still create some extra fantasy value for Irving, who is on the RB1/2 border for Week 6.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Alvin Kamara (back) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Giants.
News Snippet: Kamara played through the back issue last week, though he only saw five touches. He has fallen behind Kendre Miller in the pecking order for carries, and even CJ Donaldson is pushing him for work on passing downs. Kamara is barely an RB4 for Week 6.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Chris Olave (illness) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Giants.
News Snippet: There was reportedly a bug going around the Saints’ locker room last weekend, and Olave seems to have caught the tail end of it. He missed the first two practices of the week but was back on the field for Friday’s session. The team listed him as questionable for Week 6. Barring any further updates, we’re expecting business as usual for the star wideout. He remains entrenched in the WR1 mix for his date with the Giants.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will work out pregame to determine his status for Week 6 against the Ravens.
News Snippet: Per Rapoport, there is optimism that linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle) will be able to play this week. Judkins logged a single limited practice on Friday before being listed as questionable. The fact that the Browns are even letting him test the groin injury in warmups suggests he will miss at most one game. If he doesn’t suit up, the Browns would be down to Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime as their remaining options at running back. McLaughlin would be the better choice for fantasy managers, though this is largely a situation to avoid if possible.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is likely to play in Week 6 against the Jets.
News Snippet: The same is true of left tackle Will Campbell, who also went down with an ankle injury in Week 5. It’s a remarkable turnaround for Henderson, who was initially expected to miss multiple weeks with a high-ankle sprain. He was limited in practice throughout the week before being listed as questionable on Friday. We expect Henderson to be on a pitch count this week, but he’s still capable of breaking a long run on just a few touches. Henderson is a high-risk FLEX play for Week 6.

Headline: Jaguars declared WR CJ Williams, CB Montaric Brown, S Jalen Huskey, LS Ross Matiscik, DE Wesley Williams, and DT Albert Regis inactive for Week 6 against the Texans.
News Snippet: Jones was the only Jaguar with a questionable tag headed into this contest. Brown and Matiscik were ruled out earlier in the week and the rest are healthy scratches.

Headline: Texans declared TE Marlin Klein, S Jalen Pitre, RB David Montgomery, DE Sebastian Harsh, IOL Febechi Nwaiwu, OT Braden Smith, and OT Nate Thomas inactive for Week 6 against the Jaguars.
News Snippet: Klein remains a healthy scratch. David Montgomery was ruled out on Friday after missing all three practices this week because of a groin injury. Woody Marks will handle the lion’s share of the backfield touches versus the Jags.

Headline: Christian Kirk (calf) is questionable for Week 6 against the Commanders.
News Snippet: Kirk is a candidate to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Monday’s game against the Commanders. His status is worth tracking considering the absence of Deebo Samuel and general lack of depth at the position. Fantasy managers could be forced to wait until Week 7 for more fidelity considering the team plays in the final game of Week 6.

Headline: Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) is questionable for Week 6 against the Commanders.
News Snippet: Evans was unable to practice through Friday but ultimately did enough to land a questionable tag with multiple injury designations. However likely it is that Evans continues to play through various ailments, fantasy managers could look to make alternate plans considering the timing of the 49ers’ game on Monday.

Headline: 49ers ruled out Deebo Samuel (hamstring) for Week 6 against the Commanders.
News Snippet: Samuel will be forced to miss Week 6 with a hamstring injury sustained in the team’s Week 5 win over the Seahawks, leaving the team extremely thin at wide receiver. They could get a small boost with Christian Kirk a candidate to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Monday’s game, although Mike Evans is also listed as questionable.

Headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) will start in Week 6 against the Falcons.
News Snippet: This was expected to be the case but is now confirmed by sources close to the team. Williams returns after missing the previous three games as the Bears look to claw their way back into contention in a crowded NFC North division. Consider it a sizable boost for all Chicago pass catchers.

Headline: Patriots activated A.J. Brown (ankle) from injured reserve.
News Snippet: Brown makes his return from a four-game absence following a Week 1 injury to his ankle, reintegrating into an offense that has found their stride in recent weeks. After leading the league in turnovers through the first three games, quarterback Drake Maye has accounted for a league-leading eight touchdowns since Week 4. Although Brown could be on a snap count in his first game back, fantasy managers have to be feeling ecstatic to get their second round pick back on the field.

Headline: Eagles placed Jalen Hurts (blood clots) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Whelp, that reversed course quickly. It was reported earlier Saturday that the team was not planning on placing their franchise quarterback on injured reserve, with the team going back on those comments less than seven hours later. Although not yet fully evident, it appears as if additional information was ascertained during the day. There is no telling how long Hurts will be away from the team, with most recent reporting simply labeling it an “indefinite” absence. Tanner McKee steps into the starting role and could be worthy of deep league consideration as a QB2, for the foreseeable future.

Headline: Commanders ruled out Marcus Mariota (knee) for Week 6 against the 49ers.
News Snippet: Mariota will miss his second straight contest and third of the season when the Commanders face the 49ers on Monday Night Football. Athan Kaliakmanis will continue to serve as the primary backup.

Headline: Steelers placed Roman Wilson (finger) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Wilson suffered a dislocated finger in the team’s Week 5 game against the Colts and will now miss four games, at minimum, while on injured reserve. His absence paves the way for rookie Germie Bernard to continue to see increased opportunities. Fantasy managers can start Bernard as a viable FLEX option in Week 6 against the pass-funnel Buccaneers.

Headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is questionable for Week 6 against the 49ers.
News Snippet: Diggs returned to the practice field Friday as a limited participant, following it with another practice with the same status a day later. The listed his as questionable for Monday Night Football against the 49ers as he attempts to return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Fantasy managers might be better off playing it safe considering the timing of the game.

Headline: Commanders ruled out RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) for Week 6 against the 49ers.
News Snippet: No surprise here. Croskey-Merritt has been dealing with a groin injury since the start of the season. This week he couldn’t practice and has since been officially ruled out for the Commanders’ Monday Night Football matchup against the 49ers. Croskey-Merritt will get a two-week break with Washington on bye in Week 7. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler figure to handle the majority of the backfield touches in his absence with White being the preferred fantasy option between the two.

Headline: Pat Freiermuth (calf) is questionable for Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
News Snippet: Freiermuth popped up on the injury report Saturday afternoon with a calf injury. He’s questionable for this weekend against the Buccaneers. Freiermuth would’ve been in line for a sizable workload with the Steelers down multiple wide receivers. Coming off a two touchdown performance in Week 5, fantasy managers need a backup plan in case Freiermuth is ultimately ruled out against Tampa Bay.

Headline: DK Metcalf (illness) was removed from the injury report and is expected to play against the Buccaneers in Week 6.
News Snippet: Good news. Metcalf missed practice Friday and was listed as questionable, but has since been removed from the injury report and is expected to play this week. With the Steelers missing Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek, Metcalf could see even more targets than usual against Tampa Bay.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Ravens WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is “good to go” and should be activated for Week 6 against the Browns.
News Snippet: While nothing is official yet, Lane practiced in full all week, which is another good sign for his availability against the Browns this weekend. Lane was one of the most impressive rookies this offseason and preseason. Rashod Bateman isn’t on the injury report, but missed practice during the week with a shoulder. Lane could conceivably operate as the second option in the Ravens passing game behind Zay Flowers as early as this week.

Headline: Commanders beat writer Ben Standig reports RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) isn’t expected to play in Week 6 against the 49ers.
News Snippet: Croskey-Merritt has dealt with a groin injury all season despite playing in the Commanders’ first five games. He missed multiple practices this week and will now get two weeks off with missing the game against the 49ers ahead of Washington’s bye week. For now, expect Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler to handle the majority of the backfield touches for the Commanders.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Chargers have rejected trade calls and aren’t planning a fire sale.
News Snippet: According to Pelissero, teams have called Chargers GM Joe Hortiz, but he’s not interested in potential trade offers despite Los Angeles’ 0-5 record. The Chargers have one game left before their bye week and if they lose to the 4-0 Chiefs, falling to 0-6, this could all change. For now, the Chargers GM doesn’t want to deal, but trade calls on veteran players aren’t going to stop without a massive turnaround. Pelissero mentions Khalil Mack, Bud Dupree, Daiyan Henley, Donte Jackson, Denzel Perryman, Dalvin Tomlinson, and Tuli Tuipulotu as potential trade candidates in the final year of their contracts with the Chargers. He adds that he wouldn’t be surprised if teams that need running back or receiver help call about Keaton Mitchell, Kimani Vidal, and Quentin Johnston.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Packers EDGE Micah Parsons (knee) still isn’t practicing.
News Snippet: The Packers play the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football on NBC and Peacock in Week 6, but Parsons still isn’t practicing. According to Pelissero, it’s unlikely the 27-year-old defensive end plays before Green Bay’s matchup with the Patriots in Week 9 at the earliest. The Packers’ defense has certainly struggled without Parsons, but they have enough offensive firepower to win shootouts, which only adds to the fantasy floor for Jordan Love and Green Bay’s skill players.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) is still a few weeks away from a return to game action.
News Snippet: No surprise here. Pierce shed his cast earlier this week, but there was also a report from the Athletic’s James Boyd that he “didn’t get the sense” Pierce was close to a return. Pelissero reports that Pierce isn’t expected to return to practice next week when he’s eligible. It’s difficult to justify holding Pierce in leagues without IR spots given the circumstances.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports there’s “optimism” Baker Mayfield (thumb) will return in Week 7 against the Panthers.
News Snippet: Mayfield didn’t practice this week, but according to Buccaneers HC Todd Bowles he threw on Monday and was pushing to play before his “thumb swelled up on him.” It seems like Mayfield is trending in the right direction and that he could return against the Panthers in Week 7 if the swelling is no longer an issue. Jalon Daniels is starting for Tampa Bay again in Week 6 against the Steelers.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Eagles aren’t planning to place QB Jalen Hurts (blood clot) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: While Hurts still has no timetable to return, the Eagles haven’t even discussed the possibility of placing him on injured reserve, according to Schefter. That could change as there’s still a possibility Hurts could wind up on injured reserve if that’s where the medical information leads them. Most blood clots are treated with anticoagulants (blood thinners), which would sideline Hurts for a minimum of six weeks, according to Schefter’s sources. The best-case scenario, according to Schefter, seems to be if the blood clot is minor enough that doctors could begin treatment with anti-inflammatories. Two team doctors that Schefter polled also speculated that the 28-year-old quarterback could miss six weeks. Tanner McKee is in line to start at least a few games while Hurts is out.

Headline: ESPN’s Ian Rapoport reports the Patriots will likely activate WR A.J. Brown (ankle) to play against the Jets in Week 6.
News Snippet: Brown returned to practice this week after going on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. While nothing is official yet, it’s a great sign that Rapoport is anticipating a return for the 29-year-old wide receiver in Week 6 against the Jets. Brown may not play a full complement of snaps in his first game back, but is still essentially a must-start for fantasy managers.

Headline: Titans CEO Burke Nihill said the organization fully believes in coach Robert Saleh and general manager Mike Borgonzi.
News Snippet: The Titans are 0-5 and have won only three games since Borgonzi joined the team prior to the 2025 season. Despite this, Nihill told ESPN’s Turron Davenport that he feels a “sense of stability” in the organization. Davenport, in turn, notes that the Titans “have fired a coach or general manager every year since 2022.” Nihill apologized to Titans fans, saying ownership and team executives feel “a sense of grief” about the endless losses, and “feel the sense of responsibility to deliver” for fans moving forward. We wish them luck.

Headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) posted a video to social media indicating he will play in Week 6 against the Falcons.
News Snippet: Normally, social media posts don’t count for much. However, earlier today, Bears coach Ben Johnson said that the Bears should have more clarity on Williams’ status by the end of the day, after the medical team put Williams through “the final stress tests” in his return-to-play program. We are inferring that Williams’ social media post suggests he passed the final medical testing, though we have not officially received word that this is indeed the case. For now, we tentatively expect Williams to play on Sunday. He can be treated as a mid-to-low QB1.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the NFL “could step back in and create a longer suspension” for Josh Jacobs if the video showing his altercation with a woman is released.
News Snippet: Fowler is surprisingly saying the quiet part out loud here, though this has been the general consensus for fans and analysts for a while. Jacobs is scheduled to come off the NFL’s Commissioner Exempt list on Monday. The NFL is reportedly trying to get hold of the video, and Jacobs has sued to block its release. Fowler adds that the woman’s attorney said her client has not participated in the league’s investigation due to privacy concerns. If the video stays under wraps, Jacobs could be allowed to continue playing in the NFL.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Eagles will decide whether to place Jalen Hurts (blood clot) on short-term injured reserve on Saturday.
News Snippet: Fowler reportedly spoke to “some people who are hopeful” that Hurts can avoid injured reserve. He described the situation as being “very much touch and go” and said Tanner McKee will “probably” start multiple games. The Eagles go on bye in Week 10, so if Hurts does land on injured reserve, the Eagles’ Week 11 game against the Steelers would be his earliest possible return.

Headline: Christian Kirk (calf) was limited on Friday.
News Snippet: Kirk’s inability to practice fully despite his lengthy injured reserve stint suggests he might need another week or two to get ready for an NFL game. Still, the 49ers don’t face the Commanders until Monday night. If active, he could end up warranting FLEX treatment with Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) ailing.

Headline: Nick Bosa (calf) did not practice on Friday.
News Snippet: Bosa is on the wrong side of questionable despite prior reports and coaching comments indicating he has a chance to face the Commanders on Monday night. For now, we expect Bosa to miss another week, though the extra day off could help him return.

Headline: Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) did not practice on Friday.
News Snippet: Even for an iron man like Evans, this is a little concerning. Frankly, we still expect Evans to play, but two missed practices due partially to Achilles “soreness” are less than ideal. The 49ers face the Commanders on Monday night. Making a backup plan is worthwhile at this time.

Headline: Ashton Jeanty (foot) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bills.
News Snippet: The Raiders’ starting running back is good to go for what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment. The Raiders encouragingly stopped listing Jeanty with an ankle injury this week. Hopefully, his remaining plantar fasciitis issue subsides before long as well. Jeanty is a low-end RB1 in Week 6.

Headline: Brock Bowers (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bills.
News Snippet: One of these days, Bowers will be removed from the injury report for good. For now, we will continue to let you know that the Raiders’ star player gets a half day on Wednesday before practicing in full for the rest of the week. Bowers is the overall TE1 in fantasy football each week. Start him accordingly.

Headline: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Friday.
News Snippet: Ekeler continues to practice in a limited capacity while wearing a red non-contact jersey. He has a chance to play on Monday night, but he is clearly hurting. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) remains sidelined and Rachaad White (shoulder) has been downgraded to limited. It’s an ailing backfield.

Headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) did not practice on Friday.
News Snippet: Croskey-Merritt has played through multiple injuries this year. We still think he has a chance to face the 49ers in Week 6’s Monday Night Football game. Rachaad White (shoulder) sported a red non-contact jersey for the first time this week, and was downgraded to limited today.

Headline: Terry McLaurin (hamstring/rest) did not practice on Friday.
News Snippet: The Commanders added a “rest” designation to McLaurin’s report, so fantasy managers should not be alarmed by today’s absence. The veteran wide receiver played through the injury last week and should be expected to do so again this week. McLaurin is a WR2 against the 49ers in Week 6’s Monday Night Football game.

Headline: Ed Oliver is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Raiders.
News Snippet: Bills slot CB Dee Alford (ankle) is also questionable. Coach Joe Brady said a week ago that both players avoided long-term injuries. They might actually have a chance to play this week. Stay tuned.

Headline: Joshua Palmer (shoulder) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Raiders.
News Snippet: Palmer practiced in a red non-contact jersey on Thursday. Even if he plays this week, he is likely only relevant in single-game DFS tournaments. He mostly provides Josh Allen with another viable target on a couple of plays.

Headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Raiders.
News Snippet: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia notes that Moore resumed practicing today after sitting out on Wednesday and Thursday. He did the same thing last week before being labeled questionable and ultimately ruled out on game day. It looks like he’s a game-time decision again this week. If active, he can be started as a WR2, but re-injury remains a risk.

Headline: Free agent Terrell Jennings worked out for the Patriots on Friday.
News Snippet: Free agent running backs Ulysses Bentley and Josh Pitsenberger also worked out for the Patriots. TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Jets. Perhaps the Patriots are making backup plans.

Headline: Elijah Arroyo (shoulder) underwent further testing on Friday.
News Snippet: No update yet on what was learned, and we may have to wait until next week’s first injury report to learn more. The Seahawks’ young tight end has faced multiple injuries in his short career. Hopefully, this one is not serious.

Headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold’s starting quarterback job is not in jeopardy.
News Snippet: The Seahawks’ head coach stood by his quarterback today, saying Darnold is “definitely part of the solution” to the offense’s recent struggles.
